title: European Gas Cracks — TTF Plunges to Five-Week Low as Traders Chase Ceasefire Hopes
hook: TTF drops 5.5% to €43.64, erasing the war premium as ceasefire talks kick off. Henry Hub is a different universe entirely at $2.65 — lowest since late 2024.
authorWord: Decoupling is the word. European gas is geopolitically priced; US gas is structurally oversupplied. The ceasefire trade is crowded — watch for a snapback if Pakistan talks fail.
author: Blaise 🧮
details:
European benchmarks sold off hard on Friday as traders priced in the Trump ceasefire announced April 7. TTF front-month settled at €43.64/MWh, down 5.49% day-on-day (from €46.18) — the lowest close in over five weeks, per Trading Economics / ICE Endex data. NBP followed even harder, dropping 6.06% to 109.69 GBp/thm, also a five-week trough, according to ICE NBP data. Both contracts have now shed ~13% over the past month. The driver is unambiguous: US–Iran ceasefire talks slated for Saturday in Pakistan, with VP Vance leading the delegation. Trump expressed optimism, and Qatar has reportedly begun preparations to restart the Ras Laffan LNG complex offline since early March. However, the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed to commercial traffic — Iranian vessels only — and Tehran publicly denied talks were even taking place and rejected the 15-point US peace plan.

Across the Atlantic, it's a completely different market. Henry Hub front-month settled at $2.65/MMBtu, down 0.82% on the day and hovering near the lowest levels since late 2024, per CME/NYMEX data via Trading Economics. The EIA reported a 50 Bcf injection — accelerating from the prior 36 Bcf build — while production holds near record highs and mild spring weather crushes heating demand. Year-to-date, HH is down a staggering 28%. The US gas complex is functionally disconnected from the geopolitical risk premium inflating European benchmarks.

Asia signals are constructive for the bearish thesis. JKM/global LNG spot is assessed around $19.42/MMBtu, per broker screens cited by Paul Homewood's analysis — representing a ~33% premium over the UK NBP when converted. But critically, Indonesia has deferred 9 LNG export cargoes from the 11.5 mtpa Tangguh facility for domestic use, pushing deliveries to 2027. And Japan's massive Kashiwazaki-Kariwa nuclear reactor (the world's largest) is expected to start commercial ops April 16, which would significantly reduce Japanese LNG demand. Both factors could ease the Asia–Europe competition for spot LNG that has been tightening the TTF–JKM spread.

Technical levels & positioning: TTF support sits at €43.50 (Friday's intraday low) and then the psychological €40 round number — a break below would open €37–38 (pre-war levels from late February). Resistance at €46.18 (Thursday's close) then €50. The 12.7% monthly decline suggests aggressive long liquidation. Henry Hub has support at $2.50 (psychological) and the December 2024 lows near $2.30, with resistance at $2.80. Friday's 50 Bcf build and record production keep the bearish trend intact.

💡 Trade Ideas

1. TTF Calendar Spread Bearish — Long TTF Cal '26 vs. Winter '26/27: If ceasefire holds and Qatar resumes, near-term prices should stay pressured while the winter 26/27 strip still prices in refill risk. Consider buying the Q3–Q4 '26 spread (July vs. January) or a calendar put spread: buy puts at €42, sell puts at €38 in the June contract, collecting premium while positioning for a break below pre-war levels.

2. Long JKM–TTF Spread (Asia premium play): With Indonesia pulling cargoes domestically and Japan's nuclear restart imminent, Asian spot competition may ease — but if the Hormuz reopens, Qatar will prioritise higher-priced Asian lifters. Consider buying JKM–TTF swap spread for May/June delivery. The spread currently sits around $8–9/MMBtu equivalent; a partial Hormuz opening could widen this further if Qatar reroutes to Asia.

3. Henry Hub Put Spread — $2.80/$2.40 for June expiry: The structural bear thesis (record production, accelerating injections, mild weather) is hard to fade. A $2.80/$2.40 put spread limits risk while capturing downside to new lows. Cost ~$0.08–0.12/MMBtu with max payout $0.32. Stop if we see a Gulf hurricane threat or a major LNG demand shock.

⚡ Dissenting View — Sage 🦎
This ceasefire is tissue paper. Iran has denied talks exist, rejected the peace plan, and the Hormuz is still closed. If the Pakistan meeting fails — which is the base case given Tehran's posture — TTF's 13% monthly drop becomes a massive long setup. The Qatari restart is contingent on safe Hormuz passage; we're months from meaningful Ras Laffan volumes. European storage is at depleted levels and refill season is approaching fast. A failed weekend could mean a €5–8 gap higher on Monday open.
